newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia launches its own Peace Corps.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia launches its own Peace Corps.

text.p: Malaysia will launch its own version of the U.S. Peace Corps at the end of July, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.

Malaysia, which hosted U.S. Peace Corps volunteers between 1964 and 1983, is calling on fresh graduates and retirees to do volunteer social and educational work in the country or abroad for one and two-year stints.

"Male and female volunteers will be paid enough allowances for food and lodging besides insurance coverage and medical benefits during their stints," the national news agency Bernama quoted Anwar as saying to volunteer organisations. The programme called Yayasan Salam, or the Peace Foundation, will be officially launched on July 22.
The U.S. Peace Corps was set up in 1961 by late President John F. Kennedy. It currently has 7,000 volunteers serving in 94 countries.
